item.title: 'Unified' team beats Easton police and fire in charity game
item.description: A packed Oliver Ames High School gym cheered the Unified Basketball Team to a 48-34 victory over local police and firefighters Oct. 28 in Easton. About 300 people attended the season finale, according to a community announcement, turning the game into a celebration of the school's Unified Sports program and the student-athletes who participate in it. Oliver Ames Unified Basketball brings students with and without intellectual disabilities together on the same 24-member team, coached by Kristin Marani, who also heads the school's English Department. "This game was a blast, and the atmosphere was amazing, just as we hoped," Marani said. "We had a ton of fun. Being part of this team and being able to connect with our kids has been the absolute joy of my whole career. Thank you to everyone for the awesome turnout. And thank you especially to the Easton Police and Fire departments for taking part." Students packed the supporter section known as the "Tiger Pit," remaining on their feet and joining the Oliver Ames High School Cheerleading Team in chants. Handmade signs with messages supporting the student-athletes covered the gym walls. Players exchanged high-fives and encouragement throughout the 40-minute game as Marani cheered them from the sideline. Unified Basketball program expands at Oliver Ames The game capped the Unified Basketball Team's third season. The team played eight games this season, double the four games it played last season. Before basketball was added, Oliver Ames established its Unified Sports program with Unified Track. Unified Bocce is scheduled to join the program this winter. Marani also recognized the team's six seniors for their leadership. "I'm really proud to have those six kids," Marani said. "They've been absolutely unbelievable leaders." Before the game, team members honored Easton Public Schools employees who supported them during high school. The employees received gift bags and joined the players for a group photo. Players completing their final season also received bouquets of flowers. The game raised money for the Oliver Ames Unified Sports program. Supporters bought 120 yellow "One Team" T-shirts before the event, and raffles were held during the game. Easton police and firefighters join students on court Craig Davidson, director of special services for Easton Public Schools, refereed the game. "When we have events like this or Unified teams, it really brings so many different people together and builds a strong bond within our school community and our community at large," Davidson said. "Thank you to our Easton Police and Fire departments. They have always, no pun intended, responded to our calls for support with fundraisers and events on campus.” Deputy Police Chief Phil Adams said the event gives first responders an opportunity to connect with the community while having fun with the student-athletes. item.title: Cowardly football: Werder captain pinpoints failings after defeat
item.description: Cowardly football: Werder captain pinpoints failings after defeat Following their 1-0 defeat to VfB Stuttgart, there is palpable frustration at SV Werder Bremen over their performance, particularly in the first half. Despite having gone unbeaten in their previous seven Bundesliga matches, Bremen showed a complete lack of attacking intent and courage before the break. Werder captain Marco Friedl did not mince his words when speaking to Sky after the final whistle: “We clearly lost it in the first half. We basically played scared football. We hid when we had the ball, didn’t play good football, and then the long balls came straight back like a boomerang. Simply because, unfortunately, we were really poor.” It was also striking that VfB Stuttgart looked the fresher side on the pitch despite their preceding Champions League defeat to Galatasaray. Friedl also addressed this contrast in his interview with Sky: “Stuttgart played in midweek and generally have a packed schedule. We sat deep and went long very, very quickly and far too often, looking for ‘Fülle’ up front, which makes things incredibly difficult.” This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. item.title: ‘Let Me Just Be a Reporter for the Browns’ — Shilo Sanders Frustrated With Cleveland Reporters for Asking Shedeur Sanders ‘Stupid,’ ‘Set-Up’ Questions
item.description: ‘We Need More of This,’ ‘Making Up Fake Beef’ — NFL Fans React as Saints DE Puts Browns’ Shedeur Sanders on Notice After plenty of anticipation and debate, Shedeur Sanders finally gets his opportunity to start for the Cleveland Browns in the 2026 season. Deshaun Watson, who entered concussion protocol earlier in the week, managed to clear it late Saturday. However, Sanders received all the first-team reps during the week, prompting head coach Todd Monken to make a decision and name Sanders the starter for the Week 9 meeting with the New Orleans Saints. As expected, Sanders has already started facing tough questions from Browns reporters, something his brother Shilo believes are mostly “stupid” and deliberate “set-up” questions aimed at making the quarterback slip on a banana peel. Shilo Sanders Takes Issue With Browns Reporters’ Questions to Shedeur Sanders Ahead of the matchup, the Browns QB had a brief interaction with reporters. One of them asked Shedeur how it felt to be in a similar position to last year, taking over the starting role after initially being sidelined. “I definitely want to thank just the whole coaching staff and Andrew Berry and everybody part of the organization for giving me another chance, you know, to be here for this year, this season, and everything. Last year, I’ll say I was able to see what I needed to see, feel different things during the games, and understand what I need to get better at,” he said. Another reporter asked Shedeur, “How does this offensive system fit you?” “That’s just a setup question,” Shilo said while reacting to the interaction on his YouTube stream. Meanwhile, another reporter questioned Shedeur about hiring an agent, asking if that was “just a natural development.” The second-year QB shrugged off the question, saying it had nothing to do with the game. Shilo, however, took issue with the reporter’s approach and issued a blunt reaction. “Bro, everybody has an agent. This is another set-up question. Man, let me just be a reporter for the Browns because I can actually ask some good questions,” Shilo said on his stream. BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN’s Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator Last season, Shedeur made seven starts for the Browns, posting a 3-4 record before returning to a backup role behind Watson at the start of this season. After eight games with Watson under center, the Browns are 5-3 and rank No. 22 in PFN’s NFL Team Impact Rankings . Apart from the team’s inconsistencies and inability to make plays in the fourth quarter, one of its biggest issues has been the pressure Watson has faced. The offense has surrendered 33 sacks through eight games. Shedeur is expected to face a similar challenge and could have very little time inside the pocket when he makes his first start under center in Week 9. The Browns’ matchup against the Saints is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET on Sunday, November 8, at the Caesars Superdome in New Orleans. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Stephen Curry’s 41-point explosion prompts bold ‘so so back’ verdict from Bill Simmons
item.description: Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images Bill Simmons has declared Stephen Curry is “so so so back” after the Golden State Warriors star produced another outstanding performance in their overtime win over the Orlando Magic. Curry scored 41 points as the Warriors claimed a 126-119 victory, extending their winning streak to seven games and improving their record to 7-3. The 38-year-old has been in terrific form during that run, following up 34 points against the Phoenix Suns and 29 against the Miami Heat with another 40-point display. Bill Simmons reacts to Stephen Curry’s latest Golden State Warriors masterclass Simmons, founder of The Ringer, could not hide his excitement after watching Curry take control against Orlando. Taking to X, he posted: “STEPH NEVER LEFT BUT REGARDLESS STEPH IS SO SO SO BACK.” There is certainly plenty of evidence behind Simmons’ verdict. Curry finished with 41 points on 13-of-19 shooting, including five three-pointers from 10 attempts, while converting all 10 of his free throws. He also added six rebounds and six assists, setting another NBA record in the process. Curry has now recorded 16 games with at least 40 points since turning 35, moving clear of LeBron James, who previously shared the record with 15. His impact was particularly clear late in regulation, when he scored 12 unanswered points in the final 2:21 to help send the game into overtime. Draymond Green has seen plenty of Curry’s best moments since they began playing together in 2012, but admitted the veteran guard continues to surprise him. Speaking to USA TODAY Sports, Green said: “It never gets old. He’s so special, like, he always does something to where it can’t get old. You know, it’s always something different.” Curry was not the only Warrior to impress, with rookie Yaxel Lendeborg contributing 23 points. Brandin Podziemski also added 15 points and seven rebounds as Golden State’s bench outscored Orlando’s second unit 42-31. The Warriors have turned their season around after losing their opening three games and will now look to make it eight consecutive victories against the New Orleans Pelicans. Given Curry’s current form, Simmons may have every reason to keep celebrating. item.title: Crisis at Old Trafford! Man Utd hit 40-year low as Michael Carrick’s side drop into Premier League relegation zone
item.description: Michael Carrick Manchester United 2026-27 - Getty Manchester United have officially slumped to their lowest point in four decades after being dragged into the Premier League relegation zone on Saturday. A shock result elsewhere in the division has left Michael Carrick's side facing the very real prospect of sitting bottom of the table by the time they kick off their next fixture. Slipping into the danger zone Nottingham Forest’s shock 3-1 victory over Manchester City pushed the Red Devils into the bottom three. While the result marked a third consecutive league defeat for City, the collateral damage was felt most at Old Trafford. For the first time since November 1986, United find themselves occupying a relegation spot after playing at least nine matches. That grim 1986 campaign saw the club sitting 21st after 15 fixtures. The dismal run famously cost Ron Atkinson his job, paving the way for Sir Alex Ferguson’s arrival. Now, Carrick has overseen the club's worst start of the Premier League era, mirroring a crisis unseen in 40 years. A domestic crisis deepens The situation could deteriorate further before United even take the pitch on Sunday. If Sunderland defeat Chelsea and Crystal Palace earn at least a point against Liverpool at Selhurst Park, Carrick’s men will fall to the absolute bottom of the table. They are desperately searching for a domestic turnaround. United have not secured a league victory since a 5-2 home triumph over newly-promoted Ipswich Town on August 30. Carrick's job security has been severely tested throughout this miserable run. While a spirited 3-2 Champions League comeback against Roma on Tuesday bought the 45-year-old some breathing room, his long-term future remains precarious. A poor showing against Unai Emery's Aston Villa could ultimately force the board to make a managerial change. Carrick demands a response Speaking on Friday, Carrick insisted the European victory over Roma had lifted the mood within the camp. He stressed that the squad possesses the quality needed to escape their current predicament, even if their recent domestic output suggests otherwise. "Obviously it's a positive reaction," Carrick explained. "Again, it's not like all of a sudden we're getting carried away. I have seen enough from the players. I know what we're capable of." The manager remains adamant that his team's underlying ability is intact. "You know what we're capable of as a team. We've proved it over time," he added. item.title: ‘Like a new signing!’ - Paul Merson hails Martin Odegaard as Arsenal captain’s heroics sink Hull City to go six points clear
item.description: Arsenal FC v Hull City - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Paul Merson has heaped praise on Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard following his match-winning performance against Hull City. The former midfielder likened the Norwegian to a new signing after he secured three crucial points to extend their lead at the Premier League summit. Arsenal secure gritty Hull win Arsenal were forced to dig deep to secure a hard-fought 1-0 victory over newly promoted Hull City at the Emirates Stadium. Mikel Arteta's side looked destined to drop points before Martin Odegaard struck a decisive 72nd-minute winner. The crucial victory moved Arsenal six points clear at the top of the Premier League table. Their grip on first place was strengthened further after title rivals Manchester City suffered a shock 3-1 defeat away to Nottingham Forest . High-flying Brighton are the only side to beat Arsenal so far this season. They could cut the gap at the summit to five points if they defeat Brentford. Merson hails outstanding Arsenal captain Former Arsenal midfielder Merson was thoroughly impressed by Odegaard's match-winning contribution. Merson believes the Norwegian has been the standout performer for the north London club during the opening months of the season. "He’s been outstanding. He’s the only one really that moves it quickly," Merson told Sky Sports . "He moves it quickly, he moves, he gets into positions. I just thought too many players took too many touches and they slowed it down and gave Hull half a chance. "I think he’s been outstanding this season, he’s like a new signing for them and he’s been the man so far. Not great but just a good result for Arsenal. But again, he was one of the stars of the show." Odegaard discovers his goalscoring touch Odegaard has enjoyed a remarkable resurgence in front of goal during the 2026-27 campaign. His strike against Hull took his tally to five goals in all competitions, a massive improvement from managing six goals in 45 appearances last term. The Arsenal captain showed sharp predatory instincts to secure the victory. Konstantinos Tzolakis parried a powerful strike from Noni Madueke, but Odegaard was the quickest player to react inside the penalty area. "He’s the first one to react and there’s two defenders in front of him," Merson explained. "But because of his reaction, he runs past them, he hits it, there’s a slight deflection and it goes underneath the goalkeeper’s arms." Crucial fixtures await for Arsenal Arsenal will be desperate to maintain their momentum when they return to Premier League action after the international break. Arteta's side are scheduled to face Newcastle United in the Premier League on November 21, before hosting Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League three days later. Following that, The Gunners will take on a tough match against Manchester City on November 29.

item.title: Real Madrid midfielder highlights key to team’s success after Valencia victory
item.description: Real Madrid midfielder highlights key to team’s success after Valencia victory Real Madrid put in another convincing performance in their last game before the start of the November international break as they visited Mestalla and beat Valencia with a 3-0 scoreline . Three players who are all in very good form, Federico Valverde, Arda Guler, and Kylian Mbappe, scored the three goals for the Merengue side. Meanwhile, another player who has been gradually growing in this team and has already become a very important part of Jose Mourinho’s scheme is the midfielder Bernardo Silva, who again started this game and helped his team control the tempo from the center of the pitch. As Diario AS has reported, the Portuguese playmaker also talked to the media after the game. Silva highlighted how the physical approach from Valencia and the referee’s leniency for their fouls made this game quite difficult for his team: “It was a difficult match against an aggressive team and with a referee who allowed that aggression. That made things complicated. Fede’s fantastic goal helped us a lot. I felt that we were always in control. We were organised and managed their transitions well. We won possession back quickly, and we’re happy with the three points.” The Real Madrid midfielder was happy with his team reaching eight consecutive wins, but was clear that they will have to continue with this run of form: “It means we’re in a good position to compete. We’re very happy, but those eight consecutive wins count for nothing now. We have to keep going like this. Keep winning and winning.” Silva highlighted his team’s quality in the attack and praised Federico Valverde’s goal: “It’s simple: he strikes the ball very well and should shoot even more often. The other goals came from some great combination play involving Jude and Arda. With this team and this quality, good things will always happen.” The Portuguese veteran was also happy with his team’s defensive effort and the clean sheet: “Very important. We always know that teams who defend better are better prepared for matches and for winning titles.” The Real Madrid midfielder was looking forward to returning to play at the Santiago Bernabeu after a run of away games: “We’re always eager to return home. I’m sure the fans will be waiting for us.” There is no doubt Bernardo Silva’s presence has allowed Real Madrid to play better and this improvement is also clear from the team’s results. Hopefully, he will continue playing at this level and help the Merengues become one of the very best teams in Europe and in Spain.

item.title: Supercars Sandown: Sunday win sets up Matt Payne for title challenge
item.description: Motorsport photo Matt Payne has taken his sixth Supercars win of the season and cemented his points lead with an all-the-way – but in the end, narrow – win at Sandown Park in Melbourne. Payne put his Grove Racing Ford Mustang on pole for the second day in a row and beat Anton De Pasquale , who started alongside in the Team 18 Chevrolet Camaro, to the first corner. From there, Payne had the pace to build a gap and he did, until ‘ADP’ cleared traffic and closed over the final laps. The Camaro had the speed and started the final lap under a second behind, and with Payne facing even more traffic ahead. The gap closed, and Payne held on, to take the victory by 0.7s. As well as De Pasquale drove, second was never going to be enough for him to qualify as a finalist. Under Supercars’ Finals system, the only way he could make that move was to win the race, after Brodie Kostecki ’s Saturday win effectively meant he, Payne and only two other drivers could move forward. “That was so stressful, it couldn’t tell you,” Payne smiled after his first win since August. “I saw the train of cars, and I managed to get through some of them. We didn’t have much left at the end, but I managed to get home by the skin of my teeth We had the car speed this weekend, it was probably a little bit better than yesterday. We found ourselves a bit this weekend, we hit all our marks.” Photo by: EDGE Understandably De Pasquale was a disappointed runner-up. “I gave it everything, I was trying to hunt him down,” he said. “He got a little bit of a better one [start] and he wasn’t degging [tyre degrading] as much as I hoped he would.” Ironically, in a season in which De Pasquale has often looking like Chevrolet’s only contender, another Camaro was third. Just two weekends after he moved to the PremiAir Racing after leaving Erebus Motorsport , Cooper Murray started third and that is where he finished, after a drive that was unobtrusive because it lacked anything that looked like an error. “I am very emotional at the moment,” he grinned after the first top-three result of his career. “Second round with this team and we are on the podium. While the Spaniard has utilised a lighter schedule to implement his tactical ideas, he admits he is desperate to swap quiet training weeks for the chaos of continental competition. European ambitions at Stamford Bridge Alonso has enjoyed a productive start to life in West London, but the Spaniard is already looking ahead to a future where his schedule is significantly more congested. While the current campaign has allowed for extensive tactical work at Cobham due to a lack of European commitments, the former Bayer Leverkusen boss is eager for those "long weeks" to become a thing of the past. "The ambition is to be back there [in Europe]," said the Blues manager on the club's official website . "[We want it] to be just one season that we are having long weeks. From 2022-25, the Green Wave qualified for the conference championship in all four seasons, hosted the event three times, and captured two titles. In 2022, they earned an iconic victory in the Cotton Bowl to finish No. 9 in the country before securing a berth in the College Football Playoff in 2025, earning their second ranked finish in four years. item.title: Australia reach World Cup final after Fiji scare
item.description: Abbi Church (left) scored a hat-trick against Fiji - she now has seven tries in four 2026 World Cup matches [Getty Images] Australia (8) 30 Tries: Church 4, Upton, Chapman Goals: Kelleher 3 Fiji (8) 14 Tries: Yaranamua, Paseka Goals: Yaranamua 3 Australia have reached their fifth successive Women's Rugby League World Cup final as they seek a fourth consecutive title - but they were made to work harder than anyone expected. They had breezed through the group stages and there looked to be little to stop the procession. But World Cup debutants Fiji had other ideas. For 40 minutes, one of the biggest surprises in the history of rugby league looked eminently possible. Order was eventually restored, thanks largely to four tries from Abbi Church, which set Australia on their way to a 30-14 victory. They will face old rivals New Zealand in the final next Sunday in Brisbane, kicking off at 05:10 GMT. But having given New Zealand a scare in their opening match before losing 18-12, Fiji came out at Sydney Football Stadium fully intent to unsettle and confront the red-hot tournament favourites. In doing so, they became the first side since New Zealand in the 2013 World Cup final to open the scoring in a game against Australia, who trailed for the first time at this tournament. Church scores four as Australia beat Fiji to reach Women's RL World Cup final - as it happened The tournament debutants put pressure on the Australia line from the start. Soon the entire Aussie team caught the bug with simple drops and brainless errors, and after 12 minutes Simaima Taufa conceded a penalty under the posts. Fiji opted to kick for two points. Four minutes later, they went all the way. Captain Sereana Naitokatoka stole the ball from Jaime Chapman 10 metres from the Australia line, and they drove through the defence for half-back Luisa Yaranamua to score. She also converted to give Fiji an astonishing 8-0 lead. At last Australia sparked into life, and two tries in the final 10 minutes of the opening half brought them level. Church drove over in the right corner, before Tamika Upton slipped through the defence as Australia returned pressure following a Fiji drop-out. But Jocelyn Kelleher missed twice from the tee to allow Fiji in at half-time level. Had Upton not brilliantly tipped a Fiji grubber behind, Australia would have trailed. Whatever coach Jess Skinner said in the changing room woke Australia up, and they took control. Church completed her treble - the third a brilliant catch from a booming Tarryn Aiken kick to the corner and before grounding the ball at full tilt - either side of Chapman diving over. Normal service resumed. But at last, the Jillaroos have been proved fallible - with a late Maria Paseka try providing a deserved flourish for fearless Fiji. Church, though, had the last word for Australia - collecting Losana Lutu's kick around 30 metres from her own line before racing clear to score.

""We've been tested in a couple of ways, but there's still many ways that remain for us to be tested in," Wembanyama said. "We're in a great spot, ten games in. Season goes by quick. We're building. The common thread throughout the streak has been Wembanyama's dominance. He joined Shaquille O'Neal (1993-94) as the only NBA players to record 291 points and 39 blocks through the first 10 games of a season. Against the Blazers, Wembanyama was a highly efficient force, shooting 9 of 13 from the field, 3 of 6 from beyond the arc and 8 of 9 at the free-throw line in 24 minutes. "Victor didn't fight the game," Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said. item.description: MADISON, Wisconsin – Greg Schiano sat a table in the bowels of Camp Randall Stadium, giving his thoughts and recap of the type of game that’s happened far too often for his Rutgers football team. This one, a 31-10 loss to Wisconsin , brought a new frustration. The Scarlet Knights were competitive in the first half. They pushed the Badgers . Their offense had connected on a big touchdown against a solid defense. Then it all fell apart in the second half with Wisconsin scoring 18 unanswered points. “Second half no position (player or players) played well enough to consider winning,” Schiano said. “We got shut out 0 to 18. So no position played well enough to consider winning the game. That’s on me.” As he finished his sentence, Schiano squeezed his left hand into a fist and cracked his knuckles. Frustration continues to build. This game had plenty of it. Aside from the poor second half, Rutgers also committed costly penalties – including a roughing the passer call in the first half on Jesse Ofurie that negated an interception by JJ Conyers. That would’ve given Rutgers the ball at the Wisconsin 35. There were also two defensive pass interference calls and a targeting call on Tariq Hayer. Schiano called the penalties “inexplicable.” That could also describe this season, which started off terribly with the embarrassing loss to UMass, a loss that was a bad omen for what’s to come. At 2-7, the Scarlet Knights have no pathway to reaching a six-win season and bowl eligibility (though if there are not enough six-win teams to fill all available postseason bowl spots, teams with a 5–7 record can be selected). Little about this team showed they were capable of winning enough of their final games to make that happen, anyway. “It’s very disappointing,” Schiano said. “In my wildest expectations I didn’t think we would find ourselves here. But maybe that wasn’t realistic on my part, I don’t know. But we’re not going to be bowl eligible, that’s for sure. Mathematics tells you that.” What’s clear is that the defense was nowhere near good enough. The offense hasn’t clicked consistently.
